data.long_meaning: Veerangana is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'veera' (brave) and 'angana' (Goddess). It is believed to be the name of a brave warrior goddess. In Hindu mythology, Veerangana is often depicted as a fierce and powerful deity, who protects her devotees from harm. The name Veerangana carries the meaning “Brave Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Veerangana usually hope their child will grow to embody brave goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Veerangana was a legendary warrior queen who ruled the Chalukya kingdom in the Deccan region of India during the 11th century. She is best known for her victories against the Chola dynasty and the Western Chalukyas.

Another popular legend about Veerangana describes her as a Jain princess who defied her father's wishes to marry a non-Jain prince and instead chose to live as a warrior. She is said to have led an army of women and fought bravely in various battles during the 12th century.

On social media, the term 'Veerangana' has been used as a hashtag to celebrate the strength and courage of women, inspiring numerous posts and discussions on gender equality and feminism.
